subject: crab
pitch: A feisty red rock crab with one oversized claw raised in challenge. A wide, knobbly shell in brick red speckled with orange and cream, eyes on stalks, eight jointed walking legs with pointed tips, and claws with dark tips and little teeth on the pinchers. A tiny barnacle and a strand of seaweed cling to the back of its shell.
reasoning:
I need to plan out a TypeScript module using the SDK, sticking only to documented APIs I'm confident about, like the builder and joint creation functions, to keep the model reasonably sized and error-free.

Given the uncertainty in exact API signatures, I'll settle on a practical subset to use: part, stick, spike, rod/capsule, ring, sweep, with joints taking at/aim/dir/up/parent options and bones assigned via a bone option referencing joint handles. I'll lean on b.part applied to primitive geometries for the bulk of the body, using tubes or capsules for limbs where a direct point-to-point constructor seems plausible.

Now I'm sketching the crab's overall anatomy: a flattened, wide shell body facing forward, built from a scaled sphere, with segments for legs computed from midpoints and endpoints between joints.

Planning joint positions for the eye stalks, claw arms, and four pairs of legs, working out approximate coordinates for shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, and ankles, favoring manual joint chains over limb IK to stay safe with the API. Working out how to scatter small knob-like bumps across the shell's ellipsoid surface by computing points at various angles.

Settling on a color palette: brick red, orange, cream, dark tips, barnacle tan, and seaweed green, plus white and black for the eyes. Figuring out how to build the claw pincers from boxes and cones with small conical teeth, with a fixed upper jaw and a rotating lower jaw joint for the oversized claw, and confirming that parts are positioned in model space regardless of bone rigging, which simplifies things. Starting to write the actual code now.

Writing crab setup code...

For the pointed leg tips I'll use small cones aimed outward, with joint spheres marking the knees. I'm also setting up eye stalks as segments rising from the body with eye spheres capping each tip, and starting on the claw arm joints for the shoulders.

Now I'm designing the big left claw with shoulder, elbow, and wrist joints raised forward, plus separate upper and lower pincer joints positioned to form open jaws, then scaling down a mirrored version for the smaller right claw. Writing claw builder function...

Naming the joints with simple labels like shoulderL, elbowL, wristL, clawUpL, clawLowL. No mouth needed for a crab. For the shell, I'm placing a stretched sphere centered near the body joint, checking the top and bottom bounds so the legs still reach the floor properly.

Now I'm working out the exact scale ratios for the shell so hip joints sit just inside its surface, then scattering small spheres across the shell as textured knobs using spherical coordinates with a slight outward offset so they sit visibly above the surface. I'm treating those same small spheres as speckle details in orange and cream tones, and considering adding a front rim detail to the carapace edge.

I'm placing a barnacle on the back of the shell by calculating its position from the shell's spherical parameters, building it as a small cylinder with an optional cone-ring opening, then planning a swept seaweed strand rising from that spot with flattened leaf spheres along its path.

For the eyes, I'm setting up stalk joints on the body that connect via thin cylindrical stalks to eye spheres with small dark pupils, mirroring the right side with a negative scale. Now I'm starting to write the actual TypeScript code, defining helper functions for building coordinate vectors and adding offsets with scaling, making sure parent joints get created before any parts reference them.

Writing helper functions...

Now I'm working out the leg geometry—four pairs of hip/knee/ankle joints positioned symmetrically left and right, with segment radii and parent chains, plus cone-shaped tips at the ankles aimed downward and outward to form pointed leg ends.

Writing claw function...

Calculating teeth placement for both jaws using cream-colored cones aimed toward the opposite jaw, then capping jaw tips with dark spheres. I'm working out specific joint positions for the big claw, small claw, and eye stalks, adjusting coordinates to keep everything proportioned and above the floor.

Now I'm figuring out eye placement on the shell's front top edge using the ellipsoid surface equations, and generating a scatter of randomized bumpy knobs across the shell surface using spherical coordinates with some outward offset so they read as texture rather than sinking into the shell.

I'm working out exclusion zones so knobs don't overlap the barnacle or eye-stalk regions, then positioning the barnacle itself as a small cylinder with a dark top dot on the dome, and starting to lay out a seaweed path with a sequence of 3D points curving upward from the barnacle base.

Now I'm reconsidering the overall scale—realizing a real rock crab's carapace is only about 15-20cm wide with a legspan near 40cm, but my current proportions would make it nearly 80cm across, so I need to decide whether to shrink all coordinates to keep the model realistically sized.

Since joints above the root must stay unscaled, wrapping the result in a scaled group would break the contract, so I should instead just redesign the coordinates directly at real-world scale: carapace roughly 0.3m wide, legs spanning about 0.4m, and claw reach around 0.2m, giving a compact but still feisty-looking crab around 0.6m total with the claw extended.

Working through exact coordinates now: positioning the shell, hip/knee/ankle/tip joints for each leg, the eye stalks and sphere eyes, the asymmetric big and small claws with their shoulder/elbow/wrist joints and palm radii, plus the barnacle and seaweed decorations attached to the shell surface. I'm also mapping out the knobby shell texture using spherical coordinates, small teeth cones inside the claws aimed toward each other, and pupil spheres offset slightly forward on the eyes for a lively look. Finally I'm settling on keeping helper types loose (using inferred return types rather than importing a Joint type) and trimming imports down to just what's needed before writing out the full component code.
